rules.why: Commits go through the harness: after a passing verify, run('plan', 'step_done', {message}) commits the step's files, or run('git', 'commit', {files, message}) commits named plan files; the harness checks the change and commits it itself.

Stage files by name (git add a.py b.py), never everything: -A, --all, . or :/ can pick up secrets and files no plan names. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

The repository's own hooks always run: take --no-verify (or commit -n) out. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

git reset --hard throws uncommitted work away: keep it (git stash) or restore one file with git restore <file>. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

History on a remote is never rewritten: no --force, -f, --force-with-lease, --mirror or +refspec. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

A protected branch (project.json protected; main and master by default) is never written from here: work on a branch of the plan and open a merge request. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

The home, the repository that holds the harness, never pushes; its changes are released by the maintainer. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

Agent files (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md) never reach a remote: unstage them, or take them out of the commits to push. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.

git with a global option the gate does not follow (-c, --git-dir, --work-tree...) may run in another repository or skip its hooks: the user is asked. On a protected branch this needs the user's word: run it with run('git', 'run', {repo, args}); the user accepts it in a form, kept in SQL.
A secret never reaches a commit: take it out of the file (and revoke it), read it from the environment or a vault, verify again, then step_done.
Commit text holds no AI mark (no AI co-author or footer, no AI tool's name or address, no robot emoji) and no Mermaid diagram: write the message as the author of the change.
The message holds a word the project bans (project.json banned): say it another way.
Agent files (.claude/, CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md) never go into a unit's commit: take them out of the step (add drop-file).
